newsitem.title: USA: UPS, Challenge in air cargo cooperation pact.
newsitem.headline: UPS, Challenge in air cargo cooperation pact.

text.p: United Parcel Service and Challenge Air Cargo on Wednesday announced some leasing and freight transfer agreements designed to expand both companies' businesses.

"The agreements we are announcing here today between UPS and Challenge are part of our strategy to create an unparalleled air freight network throughout the Americas," Robert Elizondo, UPS vice president-operations for the Americas, said.

Under the new agreements, Challenge will lease a Boeing 757 aircraft with crew and maintenance from UPS. It will fly to El Salvador three days per week and Honduras three days per week, Elizondo said.
UPS and Challenge also agreed to cargo and package transfers between the two airlines, so a Challenge customer in Latin America can send freight throughout the UPS worldwide network.

Making the announcement on the baking Miami Interantional Airport tarmac under the tails of a UPS "browntail" aircraft and a Challenge aircraft, Bill Spohrer, Challenge president, said, "This is a big day for us. We may be small but we have a solid niche in the U.S.-Latin American market."

Many passenger airlines have announced alliances and analysts have long said that various sorts of alliances of cargo airlines will become increasingly common. UPS, for example, has an agreement with Nippon Cargo Airlines to use each other's networks.
"We have found a way to help each other grow stronger," said Elizondo. Both said they are looking for ways to expand cooperation.

Company officials told a news conference that Wednesday's pact was not the first step toward a merger with UPS. "There is no hidden agenda. We have no plans to merge," Spohrer said. "No plans to merge," Elizondo added.

UPS, which has 197 jet aircraft, will continue to focus on the small package product in Latin America, Elizondo said. Although UPS operate planes in Puerto Rico and Mexico, it uses common carraige elsewhere in Latin America.
Last year Challenge began leasing a UPS Boeing 767 freighter for weekend flights between MIA and Sao Paulo with a stop in Bogota.

Challenge carried the fourth most cargo through MIA in 1996, carrying 131,942 tons, a 9 percent increase over 1995 and a 7 percent market share, according to statistics compiled by the Dade County Aviation Department.

UPS carried the 10th most with 46,066 tons, up 8 percent from the year earlier for about a 3 percent market share, Dade County Aviation Department statistics show. -Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542-7706 Fax+5017
